name: Box Squat
description: A squat performed to a box or bench that sets a consistent depth and teaches sitting back into the hips.
instructions: Stand in front of a box set to roughly parallel depth, feet around shoulder width.
Sit back and down until the hips lightly touch the box.
Pause briefly without relaxing, then drive through the feet to stand.
tips: Sit back to the box rather than dropping straight down.
Keep the shins vertical as the hips travel back.
contraindications: Avoid collapsing onto the box; control the descent.

name: Goblet Squat
description: A squat holding a single weight at the chest, which loads the pattern while keeping the torso upright.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically against the chest with both hands.
Squat down between the hips, keeping the elbows inside the knees.
Drive through the feet to stand tall.
tips: Keep the chest up and the weight close to the body.
Let the elbows track down between the knees at the bottom.
contraindications: Avoid rounding the lower back at depth.

name: Dumbbell Squat
description: A back-squat pattern loaded with a dumbbell in each hand held at the sides.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length by the sides.
Squat down between the hips with the chest tall.
Drive through the feet to stand.
tips: Let the dumbbells travel down alongside the legs.
Keep the weight balanced over the midfoot.
contraindications: Avoid rounding the lower back at depth.

name: Barbell Front Squat
description: A squat with the barbell racked across the front of the shoulders, which keeps the torso upright and shifts emphasis toward the quadriceps.
instructions: Rack the bar across the front of the shoulders with the elbows high.
Brace and descend into a controlled squat, keeping the torso upright.
Drive through the midfoot to stand, keeping the elbows lifted.
tips: Keep the elbows high so the bar stays on the shoulders.
Drive the knees forward to reach depth without leaning.
contraindications: Avoid painful wrist or shoulder ranges in the rack position.

name: Overhead Squat
description: A squat performed with the barbell locked out overhead, demanding shoulder mobility and full-body stability.
instructions: Hold the bar overhead in a wide grip with the arms locked.
Squat down to depth while keeping the bar stacked over the midfoot.
Drive through the feet to stand, holding the bar fixed overhead.
tips: Keep the bar pulled back over the shoulders and midfoot.
Reach full depth only within a pain-free overhead range.
contraindications: Skip if you cannot hold a stable overhead position.

name: Smith Machine Squat
description: A squat on the Smith machine, whose fixed vertical bar path removes the balance demand of a free barbell.
instructions: Set the bar across the upper back and unrack it by rotating the hooks free.
Squat down along the fixed bar path to depth.
Drive through the feet to stand, then re-rack at the top.
tips: Set the feet slightly ahead so the fixed path matches the squat.
Use the fixed path to control depth on each rep.
contraindications: Avoid forcing depth if the fixed path strains the knees or back.

name: Hack Squat
description: A machine squat performed against a fixed sled at a fixed back angle, biasing the quadriceps.
instructions: Set the shoulders and back against the machine pads with feet on the platform.
Release the safeties and descend under control to depth.
Drive through the feet to extend the legs.
tips: Keep the whole back in contact with the pad.
Adjust foot height on the platform to suit the knees.
contraindications: Avoid painful knee ranges under the fixed path.

name: Leg Press
description: A machine press of the legs against a loaded sled from a seated or reclined position, training the squat musculature without spinal load.
instructions: Sit in the machine with the feet on the platform around shoulder width.
Release the safeties and lower the sled by bending the knees to a comfortable depth.
Press through the feet to extend the legs without locking hard.
tips: Keep the lower back flat against the pad throughout.
Do not let the knees cave inward as you press.
contraindications: Avoid lowering so deep that the lower back rounds off the pad.

name: Split Squat
description: A stationary single-leg squat with one foot forward and one behind, training each leg independently.
instructions: Stand in a split stance with one foot forward and one back on the ball of the foot.
Lower straight down until the back knee approaches the floor.
Drive through the front foot to return to the start.
tips: Keep most of the weight on the front foot.
Lower straight down rather than leaning forward.
contraindications: Avoid painful ranges at the front knee or back hip.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: A single-leg squat with the rear foot elevated on a bench, which increases the load and range on the front leg.
instructions: Stand a stride's length in front of a bench and place the top of the rear foot on it.
Lower straight down until the front thigh is about parallel.
Drive through the front foot to return to the start.
tips: Keep the torso tall and the weight on the front foot.
Set the front foot far enough forward that the knee stays over the midfoot.
contraindications: Avoid painful ranges at the front knee or the elevated hip.

name: Reverse Lunge
description: A lunge stepping backward into a split stance, which is gentler on the front knee than stepping forward.
instructions: Stand tall, then step one foot back into a split stance.
Lower until the back knee approaches the floor.
Drive through the front foot to return to standing.
tips: Step back far enough to keep the front shin near vertical.
Control the descent rather than dropping the back knee.
contraindications: Avoid painful ranges at the front knee.

name: Forward Lunge
description: A lunge stepping forward into a split stance, adding a deceleration demand as the front leg absorbs the step.
instructions: Stand tall, then step one foot forward into a split stance.
Lower until the back knee approaches the floor.
Push off the front foot to return to standing.
tips: Absorb the step softly rather than letting the knee collapse forward.
Keep the torso upright throughout.
contraindications: Avoid painful ranges at the front knee.
Reduce the step depth if balance is hard to control.

name: Step-Up
description: A single-leg exercise stepping up onto a raised surface, driving through the lead leg to stand on the box.
instructions: Stand facing a knee-height box and place one whole foot on top.
Drive through the top foot to stand up on the box.
Lower under control back to the floor and repeat on the same leg.
tips: Push through the heel of the top foot, not the trailing foot.
Control the descent rather than dropping off the box.
contraindications: Avoid painful ranges at the lead knee.
Use a lower box if balance is hard to control.

name: Pistol Squat
description: A single-leg squat to full depth with the other leg held out straight, demanding strength, balance, and mobility.
instructions: Stand on one leg with the other extended forward off the floor.
Squat down on the standing leg to full depth, keeping the free leg raised.
Drive through the standing foot to return to standing.
tips: Reach the arms and free leg forward to counterbalance.
Build the range gradually to a comfortable full depth.
contraindications: Avoid painful ranges at the knee or ankle.
Skip if you cannot control the bottom position.
